_README: Where each reasoning question came from. Read by GET /api/admin/reasoning-provenance
This is DATA, not prose in a page, and a test asserts every question in
move_reasoning.REGISTRY has an entry here -- so a new question cannot ship
without recording where it came from.
discovery_samples are the positions that PRODUCED the question. defect_samples
are positions where it was later found wrong. They are kept apart on purpose:
presenting a defect as a discovery would rewrite history in the engine's favour.
Every number here was measured. The scan that produced it is named so it can be

blocked_a_plan.title: Your own move stepped on the plan you wanted
found_by: Mohit read move 6 Nc3 of game 56b6c294 and said the card spoke the
consequence instead of the cause. Two questions answered that position --
blocked_a_plan and returns_home -- and the card shipped the symptom because
nothing in the engine said causes outrank consequences. The tiers exist
because of this card.

discovery_samples.note: Nc3 blocks our own c-pawn. True after Nc3, false after O-O -- a reason, where 'the knight comes back' was only a consequence.

reach.label: cards the splice changed, 150 games / 1,273 cards
firing cards re-verified on the board, 300 games

notes: The only question exempt from the differential test, because its third
clause IS the comparison: it asks what the better line gives us that ours
does not. A test pins the exempt set so nothing else is quietly excused.

abandoned_own_defender.title: You moved away the piece that was guarding something
found_by: Mohit flagged move 7 of his own game. The card read like a crash fallback
because that is what it was -- a sentence added at v226 to cover a gap.
The real story was that the moved piece had been holding something.

discovery_samples.note: The move abandons a defender. The shipped caption said nothing about it.

reach.label: fires on flagged user cards, 3,471 measured
claims re-verified on the board, 10 random cards

defect_samples.note: Names the queen on d6, but Nxd6+ Kf8 Nxe8 takes the queen AND the rook. The card understated it by a rook.
A 330cp bishop named on a 133cp loss -- ratio 0.4x. No ratio bar could ever have caught this one.

defect.what: 275 of its claims (10.8%) named a man when more material falls in the line.
defect.how_found: The ratio metric that found the same defect elsewhere scored this question at 0%, so it looked clean. That metric had just been shown to catch only 385 of 1,550 real defects -- a zero from a blind instrument is not evidence of absence. Re-measured by walking the line, 275 were wrong.
defect.fix: The framework rule 'the man you name has to be the man who falls' now applies to every question that declares claim_cp, so this one was fixed without a line of its own.

notes: Its own scope doc recorded, before any of this, that over 218 firing cards
16.1% came out even or ahead on material. That is the still-open question
about material claims generally, written down early and not yet answered.

pushed_past_the_support.title: You pushed a pawn past the square that would have held it
found_by: Mined from the cards the engine could not explain, in the same pass that
produced left_it_loose.

reach.label: usable
reach.n: 406 (96%) -- the cleanest question in the engine

notes: Reported from a 500-game sample as the SHAKIEST question, at 12% unusable
on 8 findings. That was noise: at 424 findings it is the cleanest. A rate
It is also the control for how the material rule is keyed. It names a WEAK
pawn, never a lost one -- its distribution peaks at -1 rather than 0 -- so
it declares no claim_cp and the material rule correctly leaves it alone.

left_it_loose.title: Something of yours was already hanging and you did not hold it
found_by: Mohit's idea: stop guessing at mechanisms and work the cards the engine
could not explain the way the Nc3 and c5 positions were worked -- read the
board, say why the move is worse than the alternative, and only then look
for the mechanism.
Eleven cards were sampled and reasoned through by hand. Two of the eleven
were the same story, and nothing in the system could see it.

discovery_samples.note: d4 is attacked and undefended before the move and after it. Rfd1 defends it; Rae1 does not. Then Bxd4.
The same shape on c3. Recorded from the mining run; the position was not kept, which is why there is no board here.

reach.label: cards carrying a man of ours attacked and undefended
of those, the better move holds him and ours does not
of those, said nothing at all before this existed
kept after insisting they ACTUALLY take him

defect.what: 962 of its claims (12% of usable) named a man worth less than a third of the loss. It was the only question in the engine that did this.
defect.how_found: Running the engine over all 18,920 analysed games instead of 500. The 500-game sample had called it the cleanest question in the registry, which was true and incomplete.
defect.fix: The man you name has to be the man who falls -- walk the line and count. 58.4% of the suspect claims turned out SOUND, the big number being the consequence of losing the man rather than more material, so the obvious ratio fix would have deleted about 560 good cards to repair about 400 bad ones.

notes: The threshold is a real break in the data, not a percentile: 63.3% of
findings have exactly zero material falling beyond the man named, and 7.4%
have one pawn more. An 8.5x cliff. The same cliff appears at the same place
in abandoned_own_defender, which is why it belongs to the claim rather than

engine_undoes_it.title: The engine's own line puts the piece back
found_by: Built alongside returns_home as evidence that a move cost time.

reach.label: usable
reach.n: 1,411 (30%) -- the weakest question in the engine

reach.label: challenged because nothing ever attacks the piece

defect.what: Seven findings in ten fail their own premise.
defect.how_found: The full-corpus scan. A 500-game sample put it at 71% unusable; the corpus confirms 70%.
defect.fix: Not fixed. It reaches no caption surface and, on this evidence, should stay that way until its premise is sound.

returns_home.title: The piece goes back where it came from
found_by: Mohit, on the Nc3 card: 'why would nC3 comes back to b1, there is no
attack on nc3 in coming future, it's safe there'.
He was right and the board agreed. Nothing ever attacked c3, so the knight
was regrouping, not being chased, and 'the move loses time' was reading a
deliberate manoeuvre backwards. That single complaint produced step 6 of
the procedure -- attack the story before you ship it -- which now applies
to every question.

discovery_samples.note: The card said the knight comes back. Nothing ever attacks it there.

reach.label: challenged because the retreat is a choice

defect.what: Claimed a direction the board never checked. Over 400 games, 423 claims said a piece was driven back: NOT ONE returned home, and 45.9% moved forward. Some were not retreats at all -- the 'chased' piece answered by capturing something.
defect.how_found: Mohit's complaint, then measured over 400 games.
defect.fix: The resolver refuses the claim when the move is a capture, and the sentence says 'chases', adding 'back' only when the piece really returns. False retreat claims fell from 423 to 307 with no direction asserted.

notes: A SYMPTOM-tier question, deliberately. It describes what happened after the
mistake, not the mistake, so a CAUSE-tier answer always outranks it.
